notes:
Critical fix release: the auto-updater on v1.0.38 and v1.0.39 was silently stuck. A user reported clicking "Check for updates" on v1.0.38, getting the "A new version (v1.0.39) is downloading" dialog, clicking OK, and then nothing happened — no Windows UAC prompt, no installer, no error. The 73 MB download succeeded every time but the install step silently failed before reaching the OS elevation prompt. v1.0.40 fixes the root cause and adds explicit user-visible failure surfacing so a future update bug can never again strand users without a visible signal.

This is a normal point release — both v1.0.39 and v1.0.40 share the `com.asasystems.terminal` Tauri identifier, so v1.0.39 users update via the in-app updater the same way every other point release lands. No manual install required. (For users actually stuck on v1.0.38 or v1.0.39 because of the bug this release fixes, the v1.0.40 installer needs to be downloaded and run manually once from the GitHub releases page; future updates will then resume working normally.)

### Root cause: latest.json signature was double-base64-encoded for v1.0.38 / v1.0.39

The Tauri auto-updater downloads the installer, then verifies a minisign signature over the .exe bytes against the pubkey baked into the running client. The signature value lives in `latest.json` (the file at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cjml34483/TradeSpace-releases/main/latest.json` that the client polls for new versions) and is expected to be a single base64 encoding of the standard minisign sig block (the `untrusted comment: ...` text + the ed25519 base64 + the trusted-comment + its base64). The Tauri client base64-decodes that field once and then parses the result as a minisign block.

For v1.0.36 and v1.0.37 the manifest was correct: signature value started with `dW50cnVzdGVk...` (which decodes to "untrusted comment:..."). For v1.0.38 and v1.0.39 the signature value started with `ZFc1MGNuVnpkR1Zr...` instead — that's `base64("dW50cnVzdGVk")`, i.e. the field had been base64-encoded a second time. Tauri's verifier base64-decoded it once, got back another base64-encoded string instead of a parseable minisign block, and aborted with the error `Invalid encoding in minisign data`. The error was logged to `%APPDATA%\TradeSpace\updater.log` (every state transition is logged, since v1.0.28) — but the error path in `run_update_check` only did `eprintln!` + log-to-disk, so the user never saw it. The dialog the user clicked through was the v1.0.27 "Check now" pre-download dialog; it fires on `download_complete`, not `install_complete`, which is why it lit up correctly even though the install ultimately failed.

What introduced the extra base64 layer: the v1.0.38 and v1.0.39 release pipelines were run partially by hand from bash because `release.ps1`'s automatic signer call had previously emitted 0-byte sigs through PowerShell pipes (an unrelated bug noted in the v1.0.36 → v1.0.39 changelog entries). The manual workflow that replaced it called `base64 < installer.exe.sig` to read the .sig file content and pasted the result into `latest.json` — but the .sig file's content was *already* base64-encoded by Tauri's signer (that's the on-disk format the signer emits), so the manual `base64` step layered a second encoding on top. v1.0.36 and v1.0.37 had used the original `release.ps1` flow (`Get-Content -Raw` reads the .sig file as plain text without re-encoding) and produced the correct single-encoded signature. The 424-char vs 412-char drift the user noticed between v1.0.36/37 and v1.0.38/39 was a coincidence of the underlying ed25519 sig payload size — both 424 and 412 are valid, but 412 happened to coincide with the introduction of the broken manual sign step, so the length difference was a useful smoking gun for the diagnosis.

### Fix in v1.0.40

- **Sign + manifest are produced from a single trusted command.** v1.0.40 abandons the manual bash sign workflow that introduced the bug. The release runs `scripts/release.ps1 -Version 1.0.40` end-to-end, which: builds the Tauri NSIS bundle (with `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` set to the contents of `~/.tradespace/updater.key`, so `tauri build` itself emits both `<installer>.exe` and `<installer>.exe.sig` next to each other inside `target/release/bundle/nsis/`); reads the `.exe.sig` via `Get-Content -Raw` which preserves the on-disk single-base64 form; writes that exact string verbatim into `latest.json`'s `platforms.windows-x86_64.signature` field. No second `base64` call anywhere in the path. The `gh release create` + `gh release upload` step uploads the same correctly-encoded `latest.json` as a release asset, and the same file is committed verbatim to the `main` branch of `cjml34483/TradeSpace-releases` (the manifest endpoint the client polls). Verification: the v1.0.40 `latest.json` signature starts with `dW50cnVzdGVk...` exactly like the v1.0.36/37 manifests that worked, and the auto-update path round-trips locally before publish.
- **Install failures now fire a Windows toast notification.** `tray-app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs::run_update_check`'s `Err` branch on `download_and_install` previously did `updater_log` + `write_last_check_result` + return — both written to disk, neither shown to the user. v1.0.40 also fires `app.notification().builder().title("ASA update failed").body("Could not install vX.Y.Z: <reason>. Right-click the tray icon and choose \"Show Update Log\" for details.").show()` so the user sees a visible signal the moment auto-update hits an error. This means a future analogue of the v1.0.38 bug could not silently strand a user — they would get a toast with the reason code immediately. The existing "update available" toast path (which fires on `update_available`, before the download starts) is unchanged; the new toast fires only on the failure terminal of the install attempt, which under normal operation is never reached.
- **"Show Update Log" tray menu item.** The system-tray context menu (right-click the tray icon) previously had two items: "Show ASA Terminal" and "Quit ASA Terminal". v1.0.40 inserts a third item, "Show Update Log", that opens `%APPDATA%\TradeSpace\updater.log` in the user's default text editor (via `cmd /C start "" <path>` so the user's `.log` file association wins, with a `notepad.exe` fallback if `cmd` somehow fails). The file is created empty if it doesn't yet exist (brand-new install case) so the editor opens to *something* rather than a "file not found" popup. The log already contained every state transition since v1.0.28 (`check_start`, `update_available`, `download_progress`, `download_complete`, `install_complete` / `install_failed`, with full error strings); now the user has a one-click path to it for self-diagnosis without us asking them to navigate to an `%APPDATA%` path by hand. The toast notification body explicitly tells them where to find this menu item, closing the loop.
- **No changes to the updater verification keypair.** `~/.tradespace/updater.key` and `~/.tradespace/updater.key.pub` are unchanged from v1.0.30+. The `pubkey` in `tauri.conf.json` (line 52) — `dW50cnVzdGVk...RUTL4NPW1dd4Qml96AoZyME...` — matches the `.pub` file on disk. v1.0.39 clients verify v1.0.40's `.exe.sig` against the same key they verified v1.0.39's against; the bug was never in the signing keys, only in how the resulting signature got transcribed into the manifest.

### Tray code path

- `tray-app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`: `run_update_check`'s `install_failed` arm gains a `NotificationExt::notification().builder()...show()` call (parallel to the existing `update_available` notification). The tray menu builder gains a third `MenuItem::with_id(app, "update_log", "Show Update Log", true, None::<&str>)` and the `on_menu_event` match gains a `"update_log" => open_updater_log(app)` arm. A new `open_updater_log` helper resolves `updater_log_path` and spawns `cmd /C start "" <path>` (Windows) with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` so the launch is invisible. `tauri-plugin-notification` was already in `Cargo.toml` from v1.0.16 (used for the existing "update available" / "update ready" toasts), so no new dependency.

### Auto-updater note

Same shipping pipeline as v1.0.30 → v1.0.39 except for the critical fix above: PyInstaller `server.exe` sidecar → Tauri NSIS bundle → `scripts/release.ps1` (single command, no manual bash sign step) → SHA256 + UTF-8-no-BOM `latest.json` → `gh release create` + `gh release upload` → identical `latest.json` committed verbatim to `cjml34483/TradeSpace-releases` `main`. v1.0.39 → v1.0.40 auto-updates cleanly because the Tauri identifier (`com.asasystems.terminal`) is unchanged AND the manifest signature is correctly single-base64-encoded.
